newsitem.title: USA: Houston traffic snarled by heavy spring storm.
newsitem.headline: Houston traffic snarled by heavy spring storm.

text.p: An unusually heavy spring storm snarled traffic and delayed morning commuters in Houston on Wednesday as bayous overran their banks and water pooled on freeways and surface streets, officials said.
Petrochemical plants were warned of possible flooding, but the storms were not expected to affect offshore oil and gas operations or shipping in the area, officials said.

Three-to-five inches of rain fell in the pre-dawn hours, and police and firefighters were being kept busy rescuing stranded motorists whose cars stalled in knee-deep water that closed major commuting routes like Interstate 10, the 610 Loop and Allen Parkway near downtown. No fatalities were reported.
"There are sections of major freeways closed, and we've got some areas where lots of cars are stalled out," said Houston Police Department spokesman Fred King.

Three-hour commutes were common heading into downtown, and the evening rush hour could hold more of the same as another wave of thunderstorms passes through southeast Texas before tapering off to showers overnight.
"We're experiencing a brief break right now, but it looks like we might see a couple more inches of rain," Weather Research Center meteorologist Mike Arellano said.
